$comment: Project security configuration consumed by security-audit.sh. Paths, patterns and thresholds live here so the scanner stays generic and the policy stays reviewable in one place.

secret_scan.description: Assignment-shaped credential patterns only - matching the bare words password/secret/token/key in prose (specs, docs, comments, this config, the audit log) is explicitly NOT a finding. Only a literal value being assigned to one of these names is.

dangerous_code_scan.description: eval/innerHTML/Function( usage under shipped extension code. Comments and string literals that merely document the absence of these constructs are not findings - only live, uncommented code invocations are.

git_permissions.note: On NTFS (Windows) hosts, POSIX permission bits reported by `ls -ld .git` are cosmetic - chmod is a documented no-op on this filesystem. The scanner detects NTFS/Windows and treats this check as informational rather than a pass/fail finding there. On POSIX filesystems, group/other write bits on .git are a real finding.
